description: Computing on data too large or too slow for one core: shared-memory parallelism with threads and locks, SIMD and GPUs, and distributed data processing with MapReduce, Spark-style dataflow and stream processing, always measuring speed-up, scaling and cost. Taught to the depth of a leading parallel and big-data systems course.
modelledOn: Leskovec, Rajaraman and Ullman, Mining of Massive Datasets
Zaharia and Chambers, Spark: The Definitive Guide
Pacheco and Malensek, An Introduction to Parallel Programming
outcomes: Characterise big data problems and choose between scaling up, scaling out and smarter algorithms.
Write correct multithreaded programs with locks and lock-free techniques and measure speed-up against Amdahl's and Gustafson's laws.
Explain SIMD and GPU execution models and write a simple data-parallel kernel.
Design MapReduce jobs over a distributed file system and reason about shuffles, partitioning and fault tolerance.
Build Spark-style dataflow pipelines with RDDs and DataFrames and tune them.
Process unbounded streams with windows and exactly-once semantics and estimate the cost of a data platform.

units.title: Characteristics of big data
topics: Volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value; where big data comes from (telecoms, mobile money, sensors, the web)
Why single machines fail: memory, disk and network limits; latency and throughput
The landscape: Hadoop ecosystem, Spark, cloud data platforms, streaming systems
Storage formats: CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC; compression and columnar layout

units.title: Parallel computing foundations
topics: Flynn's taxonomy; shared memory versus distributed memory; task and data parallelism
Speed-up, efficiency, Amdahl's law, Gustafson's law, scalability (strong and weak scaling)
Parallel algorithm design: decomposition, communication, agglomeration, mapping
Benchmarking methodology and reporting

units.title: Threads, locks and parallel speed-up
topics: Threads in C/C++ (pthreads), Java and Python (and the GIL); OpenMP pragmas for loops
Data races, mutexes, condition variables, barriers, atomics; memory models and visibility
Deadlock, livelock, contention, false sharing, load imbalance
Parallel patterns: map, reduce, scan, pipeline, work stealing, fork-join; thread pools
Lock-free queues and compare-and-swap; measuring speed-up on matrix multiply and word count

units.title: GPU and SIMD concepts
topics: Vector instructions (SSE, AVX, NEON) and auto-vectorisation
GPU architecture: streaming multiprocessors, warps, memory hierarchy; CUDA and OpenCL programming model
Writing a vector add and a reduction kernel; occupancy, coalescing, divergence
GPUs for machine learning and scientific computing; using GPUs through NumPy-like libraries

units.title: Distributed file systems and MapReduce
topics: GFS/HDFS design: blocks, replication, name node, fault tolerance
The MapReduce model: map, shuffle, sort, reduce; combiners and partitioners; the execution framework and stragglers
Algorithms in MapReduce: word count, inverted index, joins, matrix multiplication, PageRank
Limitations of MapReduce and the move to in-memory dataflow
Running jobs on a local cluster or a free cloud tier

units.title: Spark-style dataflow
topics: RDDs: transformations, actions, lineage, lazy evaluation, persistence
DataFrames and Spark SQL; the Catalyst optimiser; joins, aggregations, window functions
Partitioning, shuffles, broadcast joins, caching; reading the Spark UI; tuning memory and parallelism
Machine learning at scale with MLlib; graph processing with GraphX or Pregel-style models
Dask and other dataflow engines compared

units.title: Stream processing
topics: Bounded versus unbounded data; event time versus processing time; watermarks
Messaging backbones: Kafka topics, partitions, consumer groups
Windows (tumbling, sliding, session), state, exactly-once semantics; Flink and Spark Structured Streaming
Streaming algorithms: sampling, Bloom filters, count-min sketch, HyperLogLog
Real-time fraud detection on a mobile-money transaction stream

units.title: Data platforms, scaling and cost
topics: Data lakes, lakehouses and warehouses; orchestration with Airflow; schema evolution
Scaling strategies: partitioning, replication, autoscaling, spot instances
Cost models: cloud pricing, storage versus compute, egress; total cost of a pipeline in dollars and cedis
Performance versus cost trade-offs; when a single big machine with DuckDB or Polars is enough

units.title: Capstone
topics: End-to-end project: ingest, process in batch and streaming, store and query a large public dataset
Measuring and reporting speed-up, scaling and cost
Reliability, monitoring and data quality in production pipelines
Presentation and code review

schedule.title: What makes data big
schedule.exercise: Estimate the daily data volume of a mobile money operator from transaction counts and record sizes, then write a one-page note on which of the five Vs it stresses most.

tasks.title: Write the same 1000-row transaction table as CSV and JSON in Python, compare the two file sizes and explain the difference
Time a sum over a list of 10 million integers while growing the input and find where memory or time limits begin to bite
Compare row-wise and column-wise storage of a 1 million row synthetic table by timing a single-column average and justify when columnar layout wins

schedule.title: Parallel thinking and speed-up laws
schedule.exercise: Take a serial routine of your choice, mark which fractions are parallelisable, and predict its speed-up on 2, 4 and 16 workers using Amdahl's law before measuring.

tasks.title: Plot Amdahl speed-up curves for serial fractions of 5, 10 and 25 percent over 1 to 64 processors and read off the ceiling for each
Split a sum of squares over 1 million numbers into chunks processed by worker processes and report speed-up for 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers
Design a benchmark harness with warm-up runs, repeated trials and median reporting, then show how a careless single timing misleads the speed-up claim

schedule.title: Threads, races and deadlock
schedule.exercise: Trace by hand two interleavings of a shared counter increment, show one losing an update, then state the minimum locking that repairs it.

tasks.title: Run a two-thread shared counter incremented 100000 times each, observe the wrong total and repair it with a mutex
Step through two threads acquiring two locks in opposite order, reproduce the deadlock and fix it with a global lock ordering
Given a thread-pool program with a hidden false-sharing and load-imbalance problem, profile it, locate both causes and restructure it for better speed-up

schedule.title: Parallel patterns and lock-free ideas
schedule.exercise: Describe how map, reduce and scan would compute a running total of daily mobile money deposits, and say which step needs synchronisation.

tasks.title: Implement a parallel word count over four text chunks with a map step and a reduce step, and check it against the serial count
Step through a parallel prefix-sum scan on 16 values, record the work and depth at each level and compare with the serial scan
Parallelise a 512 by 512 matrix multiply with row blocks, measure speed-up across thread counts and explain why it falls short of linear

schedule.title: Vector units and GPUs
schedule.exercise: Explain in a short paragraph why a warp of threads taking different branches loses throughput, and sketch the memory access pattern of a coalesced versus strided vector add.

tasks.title: Time a Python loop against a NumPy vectorised version of an element-wise multiply on 5 million floats and report the ratio
Step through a GPU vector add of 64 elements over blocks of 16 threads, mapping each thread index to its data element and checking the result
Compare coalesced and strided access in a simulated reduction kernel, count memory transactions for each and propose a layout that minimises divergence

schedule.title: HDFS and the MapReduce model
schedule.exercise: Work out by hand how a 1 GB file is split into 128 MB blocks with three replicas, then list what survives when one data node fails.

tasks.title: Place the blocks of a 600 MB file on five data nodes with replication three, then fail one node and confirm every block remains readable
Write map, shuffle and reduce functions for word count over three text files and print the intermediate key groups to trace the flow
Express an inverted index and then a reduce-side join of customers and transactions in MapReduce form and verify the outputs on small sample data

schedule.title: Beyond MapReduce
schedule.exercise: Write a short comparison of a three-stage MapReduce chain and the same pipeline as one in-memory dataflow, naming the disk writes avoided.

tasks.title: Walk through an iterative job run as chained MapReduce passes, count the disk writes between iterations and compare with an in-memory version
Run a word count job on a local multi-process pool configured as a small cluster and record time for 1, 2 and 4 workers
Implement one PageRank iteration on a 10 node graph as a map and reduce pair, iterate to convergence and report passes needed

schedule.title: Spark RDDs and DataFrames
schedule.exercise: Given a Spark pipeline of four transformations and one action, draw the lineage graph and mark where a shuffle creates a new stage.

tasks.title: Chain filter, map and reduceByKey transformations on a small RDD of sales records and show that nothing runs until the action is called
Answer five aggregation and window-function questions on a mobile money DataFrame with Spark SQL and check totals against a plain Python loop
Reduce a skewed join's runtime by choosing a broadcast join and repartitioning, and justify each choice from the stage and shuffle sizes shown

schedule.title: Machine learning and graphs at scale
schedule.exercise: Argue in a short note when you would choose Dask over Spark for a 50 GB dataset on a single lab workstation.

tasks.title: Load a CSV in chunks with a Dask-style lazy frame, compute a grouped mean and compare the result with an eager pandas calculation
Train a logistic regression on partitioned data by averaging per-partition gradients and compare accuracy with a single-machine fit
Run a Pregel-style connected components algorithm on a 20 node graph, count supersteps and message volume, and relate them to graph diameter

schedule.title: Streaming foundations
schedule.exercise: Explain with an example why a mobile money event created at 23:59 but received at 00:03 must be assigned by event time, and how a watermark handles late arrivals.

tasks.title: Assign 12 keyed messages to three Kafka partitions by key hash and show which consumer in a group of three reads each one
Compute tumbling and sliding window counts of a timestamped event stream and verify the totals by hand for one window
Process a stream containing out-of-order events with a watermark, tune the lateness bound and report how many results change and how many events drop

schedule.title: Streaming algorithms and fraud detection
schedule.exercise: Compute by hand the false positive rate of a Bloom filter with given size and hash count after inserting a stated number of items.

tasks.title: Build a Bloom filter for 1000 phone numbers, query 1000 absent numbers and measure the false positive rate against the formula
Estimate item frequencies in a 100000 event stream with a count-min sketch and report the error for the five most frequent items
Build a streaming fraud flagger on synthetic mobile money events using velocity and amount rules, then report precision and recall against known fraud labels

schedule.title: Platforms, scale and cost
schedule.exercise: Price a monthly pipeline that stores 5 TB and processes 20 TB, in dollars and cedis, and note which line item dominates.

tasks.title: Use the pricing calculator to cost a month of storage, compute and egress for a 2 TB analytics workload and list the three largest charges
Configure autoscaling for a batch cluster with spot instances, replay a daily load pattern and compare the cost with a fixed-size cluster
Benchmark a 5 GB aggregation on a single-node columnar engine against a distributed run, compute cost per query and decide which is cheaper

schedule.title: Capstone pipeline and production practice
schedule.exercise: Present your pipeline in ten minutes with a speed-up chart, a cost table and one failure you injected, then review a peer's code against a checklist.

tasks.title: Add five data quality checks for nulls, ranges and duplicates to a small batch pipeline and print a pass or fail report
Run the same aggregation at four dataset sizes and four worker counts, then plot strong and weak scaling curves with a short interpretation
Build an end-to-end pipeline that ingests a public dataset, runs batch and streaming aggregates, stores results and answers three queries with measured cost
